body:
# Independent audit: contact-gradient trace and vanishing response corrections

Audited source: `candidate 79036a0d1b9e182a`, Sections 1--5, read line by line.

Dependencies checked explicitly: the effective nonregular multicontact volume identities in `candidate 1a7cfa3d1047cbae`; the own optimal-denominator floor in Section 2 of `candidate c0fc791108fc8765`; and the scope of `candidate ed103e599726c87f`.



## 1. Contact labels and the gradient estimate

The positive mixture identity implies rho_i is absolutely continuous with respect to mixed volume for every positive source weight. If an affine plane A is active at Y_i, then A>=L and the actual row barycenter gives E_rho_i A=A(Y_i)=L_i. The retained L-moment gives E_rho_i L=L_i. Hence A=L rho_i-almost everywhere.

If two active source planes had different continuous gradients, their equality set would be a continuous hyperplane of zero d-volume in EVERY sampled fiber. This remains true if their base coefficients differ. A positive absolutely continuous probability row cannot be supported there. The source thus has one continuous gradient c_i, although different base gradients may remain. At mixed-volume almost every row target, the continuous gradient of L equals c_i: a different active continuous gradient lies on one of finitely many null creases. Entire-fiber ties from base-only plane differences have the same continuous gradient and cause no problem.

These are exactly the labels available in the audited nonregular multicontact certificate. Repeated contact occurrences are allowed, and no individual cap-section centroid at each source is being inferred.

For an active source plane, positivity on B(y_i,r_s) gives

    L_i-r_s |c_i|>=0,
    |c_i|/L_i<=1/r_s.

If balls are taken open, pass to their closed radial limit; the non-strict inequality suffices. Multiplying the actual positive mixture identity by |grad_X L| now yields

    (1/M) integral_S |grad_X log L| dm
      =sum_i sigma_i |c_i|/L_i <=1/r_s.

There is no need for a uniform bound on the unscaled labels across the sequence. At each positive finite-plane parameter all expressions are integrable and the identity is exact; the right side then supplies the sequence-uniform bound.

Equivalently, in the same physical normalization B=-Delta log L/(N M),

    integral_S |grad_X B| dm
      =(1/N)sum_i e_i |c_i|/L_i <=Delta/(N r_s).

All factors of M and N are correct.

## 2. Volume normalization and the trace estimate

Since the mixed mean of log L is zero,

    integral_S |log L| dm
      =2 integral_S (log L)_+ dm <=2M log L_max.

Here L_max>=1 follows from the same normalization. It is not necessary for each fiber to have mean log L zero; the identity is used only after summing over all fibers.

A positive finite-plane parameter has a positive minimum on the compact canonical body and a positive extension to a neighborhood. Thus log L and its absolute value are Lipschitz on each body, even across PL creases. Their first weak derivatives have no extra crease measure. The chain rule gives |grad |log L||<=|grad log L| almost everywhere.

Choose any inball center o_z in each fiber. Convexity gives n.(X-o_z)>=r_b at surface-almost every boundary point, while |X-o_z|<=2R. Gauss--Green applied to (X-o_z)|log L| gives exactly

    r_b integral_boundary(K_z) |log L| dS
      <=d integral_K_z |log L| dX
           +2R integral_K_z |grad_X log L| dX.

This is an analytic estimate, not a claim that the array of independent radial motions about o_z is an admissible compatible deformation. Summing gives the printed estimate (3), and multiplication by Delta/(N M) gives (4):

    integral_boundary(S) |B| dS
      <=[2Delta/(N r_b)] [d log L_max+R/r_s].

For d=1 the formula is the ordinary one-dimensional integration-by-parts identity with endpoint counting measure. No ambient (n+d)-dimensional volume or fictitious continuous interpolation of the mixed measure is used.

## 3. Small-buffer application and exact scope of vanishing

The compact positive body setting and uniform interiority of all deepest sources provide fixed R, r_b, and r_s. The physical-parameter bound epsilon^N L<=C gives

    log L_max <=log C+N log(1/epsilon)

for sufficiently small epsilon; only boundedness of the physical parameter is needed here. The same-separator force estimate Delta<=epsilon S_max therefore gives the stated O(epsilon log(1/epsilon)) surface L1 bound.

This proves vanishing against uniformly bounded boundary tests and rules out a nonzero limiting surface measure of the scaled logarithm. It does not claim uniform pointwise vanishing at every boundary vertex, a uniform positive floor for L, or control against tests that grow with epsilon. Arbitrary affine logarithmic boundary-layer examples do not refute the estimate: the interval example with persistent endpoint mass has no such contact certificate with source marks uniformly separated from the endpoints.

The proof needs no thresholded convex speed. Separately, under the stronger physical-cone premise, the contributor's threshold test is also valid: if Xi=A+B, A>=-C_0, and every globally finite convex speed is admitted, the convex extension Phi=(B-C_0)_+ gives

    0>=integral Xi Phi >=integral Phi^2.

Thus B<=C_0 surface-almost everywhere and, by continuity and convexity, throughout each sampled fiber. In the actual density one may take C_0=beta+(N+2)Delta/(2NM). This is an additional pointwise bound, but it is not needed for the stronger L1-vanishing proof above. The threshold argument retains its physical admissibility assumption rather than manufacturing a separator from body minimality alone.

## 4. Explicit audit of Section 5's remaining corrections

The source's assertion that all other corrections are uniformly O(Delta) is justified with constants independent of the number of contacts.

First every source mark has energy bounded below by

    E_(K_p)(y)>=E_(B(y,r_s))(y)=omega_d r_s^d=:E_min>0.

For any denominator admissible on K_p, its integral over K_p is at least its integral over the contained source ball, whose infimum is the ball volume. This proves the lower bound without a continuity shortcut.

Second, the OPTIMAL projective denominator P_i has P_i>=1/N on the whole source fiber. The cited source proves this from concavity and the tangent plane of E^(1/d):

    0<E_K(X)^(1/d)
      <=E_K(y)^(1/d)[1+(N/d)a_i.(X-y)]

on the interior, followed by boundary continuity. This floor is special to the optimal denominator and is not being asserted for arbitrary admissible projective parameters.

Consequently the energy correction satisfies, pointwise on each old fiber,

    sum_(i:p_i=z) e_i P_i^(-N)/(N E_i)
      <=N^(N-1) Delta/E_min.

For the covariance term, Gamma(u_ij)=1 implies ||u_ij||<=1/sqrt(lambda_-). Both X and the ordinary centroid g_z lie in R Ball, so

    (1/(2M))sum_i e_i sum_j rho_ij[u_ij.(X-g_z)]^2
      <=2R^2 Delta/(M lambda_-).

The remaining constant has magnitude (N+2)Delta/(2NM). M is uniformly bounded below. Hence these three terms are uniformly O(Delta).

Uniform total surface area follows either from convex-body surface-area monotonicity in the containing ball or directly from the same inball divergence identity:

    r_b sum_z surfaceArea(K_z)<=d sum_z volume(K_z)=dM.

Therefore their surface L1 norms are O(Delta). Adding the trace estimate proves exactly

    integral_boundary(S) |Xi-(W-beta)| dS ->0.

No omitted source-count factor appears: the coefficients sum to Delta, and the cap coefficients within each covariance group sum to one.

## 5. What is not implied

For any uniformly bounded test array v_epsilon, the absolute correction response is bounded by its uniform norm times the last L1 quantity and tends to zero. This statement is meaningful on the actual changing boundaries without choosing a limit identification.

It does not by itself pass the cap profile W, the supporting facet selectors, or the physically admissible cone to a limiting body. Moving cap seams and normalizations still need their own convergence analysis. Neither a Gamma payment nor disappearance of the nonaffine centroid torque follows from this audit.
